title: Deep-dive #4 of 4 (honorable mention) — Candidate D: Disaster-Recovery Playbook Expansion. PROP-051 covers the workspace-sync mass-delete shape. Pick the 2 MOST-LIKELY remaining disaster shapes from a candidate list and author propose-only playbooks (detect + diagnose + recover + verify) for each.
context:
Per PROP-116 honorable_mention. Tail-risk insurance — the value pays off if-and-only-if one of these shapes manifests, but it's cheap to author and the active period is when we'd actually need them ready-to-hand.

Candidate disaster shapes (from DIRECTIVE-20260628-001 Candidate D scoping):
  (a) Chronic decider 403 cascade — multiple consecutive decider pushes 403 (post-Devilwench era; would manifest as stranded-patches sentinels piling up).
  (b) FUSE total unmount — workspace folder becomes inaccessible mid-run. Agents that read prompts from FUSE fail to start.
  (c) GitHub API outage — push and clone both unavailable. Agents already started run on stale state.
  (d) PAT revoked mid-pipeline — every agent's auth fails simultaneously. Like the 2026-06-22 PAT expiry but without operator pre-notice.
  (e) Integrity false-negative on a real drift — integrity reports 'all checks pass' while the site has actual broken structure (e.g., the silent-fail mode we saw 2026-06-22).
  (f) Prune-integrity over-deletes despite the 2000 cap — script bug or eligibility-classification bug.

Tinker picks the 2 most-likely shapes and authors playbooks. The selection criterion is LIKELIHOOD given current pipeline state — not severity (severity is universally high for all six).

Note: this is honorable-mention because PROP-116 ranked it #4 below the top 3. Operator may choose to skip if (1) active period returns before this directive's turn, or (2) deep-dives A or B surface enough disaster-shape candidates to fold tail-risk into them. If skip, operator marks this directive 'superseded' with the reason.
task: Execute Candidate D per PROP-116 honorable mention. Produce: (1) brief selection rationale for the 2 chosen disaster shapes — likelihood given current pipeline state, evidence cited; (2) per-shape playbook with: DETECT (what sentinel/alert fires), DIAGNOSE (operator commands to confirm), RECOVER (step-by-step procedure with operator escape-hatch references where applicable — Git Data API, allow_cowork_file_delete, etc.), VERIFY (acceptance criterion that recovery completed); (3) save as monitor/tinker/disaster-playbooks/<shape>.md or similar.
deliverable_acceptance_criteria: Selection rationale exists and cites concrete evidence (cost-history rows, sentinel files, log patterns).
Each playbook has all 4 sections (DETECT, DIAGNOSE, RECOVER, VERIFY).

Recovery procedures reference existing operator escape hatches where applicable (Git Data API push-via-api.js, allow_cowork_file_delete, push-failure-archive.jsonl, etc.) rather than reinventing them.
If a chosen shape lacks a clear DETECT mechanism, the playbook explicitly says 'no current canary — recommend authoring one' with the canary specification.
If tinker thinks PROP-116's likelihood ranking is wrong, propose an updated ranking in the report and explain why.
constraints: Propose-only on any new sentinel canary specifications.
Standalone deep-dive — last in the sequence; no further directives queued.

Don't author playbooks for shapes that already have one (e.g., PROP-051 covers (a)+(b) shape variants; if tinker thinks the existing playbook is adequate, say so and pick different shapes from the list).
Tail-risk discipline: 2 playbooks, not 6. The point is the highest-value insurance, not exhaustive coverage.
